programme: HAND2, NEUROD1 and SOX10 form the neural-crest/neuroendocrine lineage-specification arm: HAND2's target set directly includes TH and DBH (catecholamine-synthesis enzymes) and PHOX2B (autonomic neuron identity), NEUROD1 drives neurogenic/dopaminergic reprogramming, and SOX10 specifies myelinating oligodendrocyte/Schwann-cell identity. SOX5, HOXA5, DMRT1, PITX2 and PLAG1 form the second arm: developmental differentiation genes whose loss (by CpG methylation or circRNA/miRNA-sponge suppression) releases EMT machinery (SOX5's targets include CDH1, CDH2 and TWIST1). The two arms are the same phenomenon read in two tissues: a lineage-restriction TF set that keeps a cell terminally differentiated.
role_in_a: In Parkinson's disease this module maintains dopaminergic/catecholaminergic neuron identity and the oligodendrocyte support network around it. NEUROD1 is used experimentally to push cells toward a dopaminergic fate (28398344) and to drive dopaminergic neurogenesis via Wnt signalling (30176346); SOX10-linked oligodendrocyte programmes are disrupted in the PD cingulate cortex and rescuing them ameliorates myelin impairment in PD models (35394697, 40801579). HAND2's canonical transactivation of TH/DBH (visible in its own target list here) is the expected upstream link to dopamine/noradrenaline synthesis, though no PD-specific citation for HAND2 itself was retrieved.
role_in_b: In gastric cancer this module acts as a differentiation brake on epithelial-mesenchymal transition. SOX5 is silenced and functionally required to be lost for gastric cancer proliferation and glycolysis (39278782); DMRT1 is one of the classic genes epigenetically silenced by CpG methylation in gastric carcinoma (19195878); PLAG1 is suppressed via a circRNA-miRNA sponge axis that drives chemoresistance (36624091); PITX2 is targeted mechanistically in a study of SASP-mediated gastric cancer progression (40995693); NEUROD1 itself is also implicated via miR-374a-5p in gastric cancer diagnosis/resistance (31614322).
shared_axis: Both diseases reflect failure of the same class of terminal-differentiation transcription factors to hold a cell state: in PD, loss/dysfunction of HAND2-NEUROD1-SOX10 activity tracks with dopaminergic neuron death and demyelination; in gastric cancer, epigenetic silencing of SOX5/HOXA5/DMRT1/PITX2/PLAG1 removes the same class of lineage-restriction genes and permits EMT. This is a convergent 'loss of an identity-maintenance TF programme' mechanism operating independently in two tissues, not a shared causal pathway between the diseases.
reasoning: The module is nameable and each arm has direct, on-topic citations in its own disease (NEUROD1/SOX10 in PD; SOX5/DMRT1/PITX2/PLAG1/NEUROD1 in gastric cancer), so this clears 'supported' rather than 'unexpected'. It stays at 'moderate' rather than 'strong' because the single best-recurring factor, HAND2 (186/270), has no PD-specific citation at all — its role there is inferred from its own target list, not documented — and no retrieved source connects the two diseases through this programme jointly.
support: 28398344 — NEUROD1 used to induce dopamine neurons from astrocytes, supporting a direct dopaminergic-reprogramming role in PD; 30176346 — NEUROD1 linked to Wnt-driven dopaminergic neurogenesis in a PD model; 40801579 — restoring an oligodendrocyte transcriptional programme (SOX10 lineage) ameliorates myelin impairment in PD models; 35394697 — SOX10-associated myelination network is disrupted in PD cingulate cortex; 39278782 — SOX5 is directly regulated (via circRNA sponge) to control gastric cancer proliferation/glycolysis; 19195878 — DMRT1 is epigenetically silenced by CpG methylation in gastric carcinoma; 36624091 — PLAG1 axis drives malignant phenotype and chemoresistance in gastric cancer; 40995693 — PITX2 is a direct mechanistic target in gastric cancer progression; 31614322 — NEUROD1 implicated via miR-374a-5p in gastric cancer diagnosis/resistance.
how_to_falsify: In iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons (PD patient vs control lines), run ChIP/CUT&RUN for HAND2 at the TH and DBH promoters and knock down HAND2/NEUROD1/SOX10 to see if TH, DBH and myelin genes drop as predicted; separately, bisulfite-sequence the SOX5, DMRT1, PITX2 and PLAG1 promoters in matched gastric tumour/normal pairs and re-express each in a silenced gastric cancer line to see if CDH2/ZEB1/TWIST1-pathway EMT markers and invasion fall. If HAND2 does not occupy TH/DBH, or re-expression of the cancer-arm factors does not suppress EMT markers, the shared-programme account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing here is blood (as PD proxy) vs stomach — genuinely different tissues, so this is a convergent-mechanism argument, not a shared-tissue one. 270 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the large denominator overstates independence. ESR1 recurred at 148/270 but is flagged discordant (its target sets did not agree between the diseases) and was deliberately excluded. NFIA and CAMTA1 recurred concordantly but carry no on-topic citation in either disease and were left out; PMID 27100827 does describe a real PD/H. pylori-gastric mucosal link, but through autoimmunity, not through NFIA's regulatory targets, so it is not mechanistic support for this module. GLI3 shares thematic ground (SHH is both a GLI3 partner and a HAND2 target) but has zero retrieved citations and was excluded as a carrying factor. TWIST1 and JUN, the obvious 'master EMT/AP-1' reach, are both single-view and tissue-generic — their absence is by design, not an oversight.
